2027-07-12.title: Second Monday of Kaitha
2027-07-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The crown of life for those who endure the trial
Those who do the will of God enter the Kingdom
2027-07-12.alt: Season of Kaitha (Qaita, Summer), which began on Sunday 4 July: after the apostles have sown the Gospel, the Church looks at its growth and fruit. This is the season of the apostles and martyrs who watered the Church with their blood, and of watchfulness for the coming of the Lord. The Fridays of Kaitha remember martyrs and saints of the East Syriac tradition. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari. The calendar's own headings: “The crown of life for those who endure the trial”; “Those who do the will of God enter the Kingdom”. In the Latin calendar today is the Monday of the fifteenth week in Ordinary Time (the readings there begin the book of Exodus); St Benedict was remembered yesterday.
2027-07-12.verse: Blessed is anyone who endures temptation. Such a one has stood the test and will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.
theo: The letter of James opens its first chapter with a blessing for those who hold on: “Blessed is anyone who endures temptation. Such a one has stood the test and will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.” The Greek word means both a trial and a temptation; it is the same test seen from two sides, depending on what the person does with it. The crown of life is the wreath that is given to the athlete who has finished the race, here the life of God himself, promised to those who love him. Then James has to be careful, because people in trouble are quick to blame God. “No one, when tempted, should say, ‘I am being tempted by God’; for God cannot be tempted by evil and he himself tempts no one.” God may test, as he tested Abraham, in order to strengthen; he never draws anyone towards sin. The Lord's Prayer asks the Father, “Lead us not into temptation”, and the Catechism explains that this is a prayer that the Spirit may help us tell a trial that makes us grow from a temptation that leads to sin and death (Catechism 2846–2847).

Then James gives the anatomy of a fall, as in a pregnancy: “But one is tempted by one's own desire, being lured and enticed by it; then, when that desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin, and that sin, when it is fully grown, gives birth to death.” Desire is the bait, and the fish is hooked by what it wants. Nothing happens suddenly: the thought, the consent, the act, the habit, and finally death. The sentence is a mirror held up to a Kerala household. The glance at the phone that becomes a hidden habit, the first drink, the first small lie about money, the first bitter word that becomes silence at the table: each grows. And against this birth that ends in death, the apostle places another birth. “In fulfillment of his own purpose he gave us birth by the word of truth, so that we would become a kind of first fruits of his creatures.” Desire gives birth to death; God gives birth to us by his word, which is truth. The second birth is baptism and the faith that comes by hearing the Gospel.

Between the two births stands the great sentence on God's character: “Every generous act of giving, with every perfect gift, is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow due to change.” The sun, the moon and the stars change, and the monsoon sky is never the same for two hours together, with its light and shadows. The Father of lights does not change. Everything good that reaches us, a child's birth, a harvest, a healing, the forgiveness of sins, comes from him, and he never takes back what he gave. And we are “first fruits”. In Israel the first sheaf of the harvest was brought to the priest and offered to God (Leviticus 23:10) as the sign that the whole harvest belongs to him. In this season of Kaitha, when the Church looks at her growth and fruit, James tells us that the baptised are that offering: the first of a harvest that will include the whole creation.

The Gospel is the end of the Sermon on the Mount, and it is a test of everything we have heard so far. “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.” Even prophesying, casting out demons and deeds of power in his name are not a passport if there is no obedience. The words “I never knew you” are terrible, and they should be read alongside the Father's own way of knowing, which is loving. Then comes the parable known to every child in Kerala. Two houses stand through the same weather: “The rain fell, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house.” We have lived this: the great floods of 2018 showed us what is carried away and what stands. The house on rock stands, and the house on sand falls “and great was its fall!” The only difference is that one builder “hears these words of mine and acts on them”. The rock is Christ and his word, and building on the rock means acting on it, in small things on an ordinary Monday: the honest day's work, the forgiveness offered, the prayer kept. “Now when Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astounded at his teaching.” The crowd was astonished, but the wise man built.
outline: Two houses, one storm: what is under the floor?
Blessed are those who endure; God tests but never tempts.
Desire gives birth to sin and death; God gives birth to us by the word of truth.
Every good gift from above; no shadow of change; first fruits.
Not those who say Lord, Lord, but those who do the Father's will; hearing and acting.
“Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.”
live: Name one desire that is beginning to lead you into sin and stop it at the first thought, with a short prayer: ‘Lord, help me.’
Each evening this week write down three good gifts from the Father of lights and thank him.
Choose one saying of Jesus, such as ‘forgive’, and do it this week in a concrete way.
fathers: Whoever hears the words of the Lord and does them builds on rock; whoever hears them and does not do them builds on sand. It is not enough to hear. The rock is the firmness of doing what the Lord has commanded.

Do not think that it is enough to say Lord, Lord, or to have done great things in his name. What matters is the life that follows the word. For faith without works is dead, and works are the proof that the faith is alive.
magis: God tempts no one to evil; in the Lord's Prayer we ask not to be led into temptation, and the Holy Spirit helps us to tell the trial that makes us grow from the temptation that leads to sin and death.
The will of the Father is that all be saved; we ask in the Our Father that his will be done on earth as it is in heaven, and we do it by joining ourselves to the obedience of Jesus.
All Christians, in any state or walk of life, are called to the fullness of Christian life and to the perfection of charity.
saints: Second Monday of Kaitha. In the Latin calendar, the Monday of the fifteenth week in Ordinary Time. St Benedict, patron of Europe, was remembered yesterday, and the Benedictine motto “Ora et labora”, prayer and work, is a good commentary on today's Gospel.

7–12 July: first week and second Sunday of the Season of Kaitha. Fri 9: First Friday of Kaitha, Saint James of Nisibis (Mar Yakob). Sun 11: Second Sunday of Kaitha (in the Latin calendar the Fifteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time; St Benedict gives way to the Sunday). Looking ahead: Thu 15, Sts Kuriakose and Julitta; Fri 16, Our Lady of Mount Carmel and Mar Mari, disciple of Mar Addai.
2027-07-12.prayer: Father of lights, from whom every good gift comes down and with whom there is no change, we thank you for the gift of life, of faith and of every blessing of this day. Keep us in time of trial, and let us never say that you tempt us. When desire lures us, give us the grace to turn from it at the first thought. You have given us birth by the word of truth: make us the first fruits of your creation, a harvest that is pleasing to you. Teach us not only to say, ‘Lord, Lord’, but to do your will, and set the house of our family, our parish and our heart upon the rock of your Son, so that in the rain and the flood and the wind we may stand. We ask this through Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, one God, for ever and ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we hear the word, which is the first work, and then we stand at the altar, where Christ himself, the rock, gathers his Church. The Body and Blood of the Lord are the gift from above, the Father's generous gift that never changes. We receive him so that we may carry what we have heard into the ordinary week and build upon it.

quick: James: blessed is the one who endures; God tempts no one; desire gives birth to sin and sin to death.
James: every good gift comes from the Father of lights, who does not change; he has given us birth by the word of truth, as first fruits.
Matthew: not those who say Lord, Lord but those who do the Father's will; the wise man builds his house on rock, and acts on the words.
2027-07-12.action: Choose one word of Jesus and put it into practice at home today, in a visible, small deed.
2027-07-12.question: What is the foundation of my house, and what happens to it in a storm?

family.explain: Jesus told us about two builders. One built his house on rock, and the other built his on sand. When the rain and the floods and the wind came, the house on the rock stood, but the house on the sand fell down. The rock means listening to Jesus and doing what he says. Every time we obey Jesus, our family house becomes stronger.
family.intention: We pray for families who lost their houses in floods and landslides, and for those who build and repair houses.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus asked us to do that our family can do this week?”

illus: A mason in Kuttanad (a story told to illustrate the reading), who rebuilt houses after the 2018 floods, always insisted on digging down to the hard soil before laying a single stone, even when the owner was in a hurry and wanted to see walls. ‘The wall that people see is a month's work,’ he would say, ‘the part they do not see is where the house is saved or lost.’ A young helper once asked why he took so long over the foundation. The mason pointed to a house nearby that had shifted after one heavy rain. ‘That one hurried,’ he said. When the next flood came, his houses stood with water around them. The helper, who had joined the church choir that year, said afterwards, ‘Now I understand the Gospel about the rock; I only had not seen it with my own hands.’

pm.open: Father of lights, giver of every good gift, you do not change. Teach us to hear your word and do it, and let our house stand on the rock. Amen.
share: Blessed is anyone who endures temptation (James 1:12). What trial am I enduring now, and how can I stay faithful in it?
Desire gives birth to sin (James 1:15). Which desire is growing in me, and what is the first step I can take against it?
Every perfect gift is from above (James 1:17). Which gifts have I forgotten to thank him for?
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord’ (Matthew 7:21). What do I say to the Lord, and what do I actually do?
pm.resp: Lord, give us the grace to hear and to do.
interc: For those in trial and temptation, that they may endure and receive the crown of life.
For young people, that they may be saved from the first bait of sin.
For families rebuilding after floods and storms, that they may be supported.
For preachers and teachers, that their lives may match their words.
For ourselves, that we may build our houses on the rock of his word.
pm.close: Father, you have given us birth by the word of truth. Make us hear it and do it, until we stand with you for ever, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the Apostle James says: “Blessed is anyone who endures temptation” (James 1:12). Every one of us has trials, in health, in the family, in work. If we stay faithful, we will receive “the crown of life”. But James also says something we must never forget: God does not tempt anyone. When we fall, we must not say, ‘God tempted me.’

James shows us how sin grows: first a desire, then a consent, then the act, and then the habit, and finally death. So we must stop it at the first step. When a bad thought comes, say a short prayer, and turn. And against the birth that ends in death, God gives us another birth: “he gave us birth by the word of truth” (James 1:18). We are his first fruits.

James also tells us that every good gift comes from above, from the Father of lights, who never changes (James 1:17). In these days of monsoon, when the sky changes every hour, it is good to remember that our Father does not change. Let us thank him each evening for three gifts.

In the Gospel Jesus says: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father” (Matthew 7:21). It is not enough to say the right words. We must do what he says.

Two houses, one rain. Everyone who hears his words and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on rock (Matthew 7:24). In 2018 Kerala saw what the flood does to a house with no foundation. Let us build on the rock this week by doing one thing that the Lord has said. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about two houses. The wise man built his house on rock, and the foolish man on sand. When the rain and the floods came, the house on the rock did not fall! When you listen to Jesus and do what he says, you are building on rock. Be kind, tell the truth, say your prayers, and help at home. Then, when something hard comes, you will stand strong, just like the house on the rock.

intro: Theme: “Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.”
Trial and temptation, the two births, the Father of lights and his first fruits, and the house on the rock.

points.h: Blessed is the one who endures
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither.
Blessed is anyone who endures temptation. Such a one has stood the test and will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.
points.apply: Stop one growing desire at its first thought, with a short prayer.

q: The Lord will give what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
In fulfillment of his own purpose he gave us birth by the word of truth, so that we would become a kind of first fruits of his creatures.

sub: Not those who say Lord, Lord.
q: The Lord is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, my God, my rock in whom I take refuge.
Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.

concl: The Father of lights gives us birth by his word and tests us in order to strengthen us, and never tempts us.
The wise build on the rock by doing what he says.
2027-07-12.resolve: This week, cut one temptation early, count three gifts each night, and do one word of the Lord.
